explanation_used: If one has strong willpower, a way opens up even for a difficult task.
proverb: Where there's a will, there's a way

explanation_used: Only by working hard does one get a good life or a reward.
proverb: If the hand gets muddy, the mouth gets curd

explanation_used: Staying silent as the situation demands is more valuable and wiser than speaking unnecessarily.
proverb: Speech is silver, silence is gold

explanation_used: Not everything that looks attractive or pure on the outside is truly good or valuable.
proverb: Not everything white is milk, not everything that shines is gold

explanation_used: Any matter or bad habit should be corrected early, at a young age; once one is older or time has passed, correcting it is impossible.
proverb: What doesn't bend as a sapling, will it bend as a tree?

explanation_used: In any system or job, only one who understands the hardships and losses at the lower level and has served honestly becomes worthy of being a good leader or officer in the future.
proverb: One who can be a servant can become a king

explanation_used: Only those who maintain patience and restraint in difficult situations or hard times find success and peace in life.
proverb: One who endures will thrive

explanation_used: When a highly valuable object, authority or responsibility is given to a person without worthiness or qualification, they waste it without knowing its true value or use.
proverb: Like giving a ruby to a monkey's hand

explanation_used: Proverbs born from long human experience and truth never become false in any age; they are always true.
proverb: Even if the Veda proves false, the proverb will not

explanation_used: One should spend, or hold desires, only in line with one's income, wealth or capacity.
proverb: Stretch your legs only as far as the bed allows

explanation_used: A person has to experience for himself the good or bad result of the work, deeds or effort he has done.
proverb: Eat what you have made, O lord (you reap what you sow)

explanation_used: Excessive desire or greed is never good; it leads a person to destruction.
proverb: Excessive desire leads to a bad end

explanation_used: The basic nature or bad habits of some people never change no matter how much one tries.
proverb: A dog's tail is crooked

explanation_used: It is not right for any person or organization to show partiality or discrimination among people.
proverb: Butter for one eye, lime for the other eye

explanation_used: Qualities or habits that come from birth do not change until the end of a person's life.
proverb: Inborn nature doesn't go even if burned

explanation_used: When hard times or a bad situation arrive, a person's mind doesn't work and he makes wrong decisions.
proverb: At the time of destruction, a perverse mind

explanation_used: By travelling the world to gain experience and by reading good books, a person gains complete knowledge.
proverb: Travel the country and see, read the books and see

explanation_used: Deliberately bringing upon oneself a trouble or danger that has nothing to do with one.
proverb: Like inviting into your house the calamity (Mari) passing by on the street

explanation_used: One who has done a wrong or improper act must face its consequences.
proverb: After eating salt, one must drink water

explanation_used: Spending lavishly and making merry with others' money without any accounting.
proverb: Yellamma's fair on someone else's money

explanation_used: This proverb expresses the assurance that whatever happens in life ultimately turns out for the good.
proverb: Everything that happens is for the good

explanation_used: One should adapt oneself to changing times and circumstances.
proverb: Walk according to the times, dance according to the beat

explanation_used: A warning that one shouldn't greedily eye the house or property one's elder brother built with hardship.
proverb: Don't burgle the house that fed you

explanation_used: Every greedy person keeps his eye on whatever benefits him.
proverb: Mari's eye is on the bull, the butcher's eye is on the sheep

explanation_used: Whatever comes to one's share, one should accept it happily (what comes to one's lot is paramanna).
proverb: What comes to one's lot is paramanna (sweet rice pudding)

explanation_used: A saying that a little exaggeration or even a lie is no sin if it brings about a wedding, which is a good-intentioned act.
proverb: Tell a thousand lies and perform one wedding

explanation_used: A warning not to trust a shrewd and scheming person; it is also an old, conventional prejudice against short people.
proverb: Even if you trust a thief, don't trust a short man

explanation_used: Not admitting one's defeat and showing off even after losing or being humiliated.
proverb: Though he fell to the ground, his moustache didn't get dirty

explanation_used: One cannot know a person's inner nature or hidden danger from outward appearance; one can't say what is hidden in whom.
proverb: Which snake is in which anthill

explanation_used: Even if the higher authority or the god himself agrees, the intermediary or subordinate in between creates obstacles.
proverb: Even if the god is pleased, the priest isn't

explanation_used: The meaning may be that people know the inner truth of their own house or matter well enough themselves and have no need of outsiders' talk.
proverb: We know the truth of our own god

explanation_used: The wording is unclear; it may mean that one dubious matter is backed by an equally dubious witness.
proverb: For the bitter gourd, the neem fruit is the witness

explanation_used: An opportunity or gain slips away at the last moment, just as it was about to be obtained.
proverb: The morsel that came to the hand didn't reach the mouth

explanation_used: The unexpected, happy coincidence when what one wanted is exactly what others say as advice or orders.
proverb: What the patient wanted was milk-rice; what the doctor prescribed was milk-rice

explanation_used: One who has done wrong always finds some small excuse to escape.
proverb: A thief always has a petty excuse

explanation_used: Blaming equipment or circumstances instead of accepting one's own incompetence or shortcoming.
proverb: The woman who couldn't dance said the floor is crooked

explanation_used: Returning in vain, empty-handed just as one went, without any gain.
proverb: Putta went, Putta came back.

explanation_used: A saying about people who cause absurd disruption in the middle of a sacred or orderly event.
proverb: Like letting a bear loose during Shiva worship

explanation_used: A guilty person takes others' ordinary words as being about himself and gives away his own crime.
proverb: Say 'pumpkin thief' and he felt his own shoulder

explanation_used: Giving a roundabout, needlessly twisted answer to a simple question, or saying something obvious in another way.
proverb: 'Malli, Malli, how many legs does the cot have?' 'Three and one more,' she said

explanation_used: This proverb says a wrongdoer's mind is always full of fear and suspicion and startles at the slightest sound.
proverb: A thief's mind is jittery

explanation_used: If a great danger that was about to strike narrowly misses, it is like getting a new life; a consoling word that one will live long.
proverb: If the swinging club misses, a hundred years of life

explanation_used: A woman who is won over with love is an affectionate woman; if angered she takes a terrifying form.
proverb: If a woman is won over she is a woman, if angered she is a fearsome goddess.

explanation_used: When two people work together, one pulls in one direction and the other in the opposite direction, spoiling the work.
proverb: When the ox pulled uphill, the buffalo pulled into the water

explanation_used: When a new attraction or relationship comes along, one should not forget those who fed and raised one in hard times or did one favors.
proverb: Though the one who gives kisses has come, don't forget the one who gave you morsels

explanation_used: A proverb in a local dialect whose words are unclear; guessed to mean wavering, uncertain behavior and not standing by one's word (uncertain).
proverb: The god of Sindhaghatta wavers back and forth

explanation_used: Bringing an unrelated matter into an unrelated place; that is, an irrelevant remark.
proverb: What relation is there between Gokulashtami and Imam Saab?

explanation_used: One who works humbly like a servant today will one day rise to a higher position.
proverb: One who lives as a servant today will be a king tomorrow

explanation_used: Every house has some problem or shortcoming; nobody's house is perfect.
proverb: Everyone's house has holes in the dosa

explanation_used: A remark that the son-in-law is not like one's own son but has come only through the relationship of being the daughter's husban.
proverb: Not a son-in-law, just the daughter's husband

explanation_used: A saying about those who are like a sweet parrot when treated lovingly and like a tormenting cobra when provoked .
proverb: If played with, a parrot; if provoked, a cobra

explanation_used: The emotion of a man who weeps excessively or a woman who laughs excessively may be put on, so one should not blindly trust such people's words.
proverb: Don't trust a weeping man or a laughing woman

explanation_used: Even one word of sympathy gives great courage and comfort to those in trouble.
proverb: Saying 'oh, poor thing' is half a lifespan

explanation_used: The one who does wrong has no shame, but those who watch it feel embarrassed.
proverb: If the performer performs, the onlooker feels shame

explanation_used: Another small trouble comes to one already in fear or hardship and unnerves him further.
proverb: Like a frog jumping on one who is already frightened

explanation_used: It may mean that on seeing a bad omen or sign of danger, one should wake up and be alert rather than lie down and ignore it.
proverb: If you see a bad dream, get up and sit

explanation_used: It may mean an arrangement that is equally useful to both sides, or one that favors neither side.
proverb: Like placing a lamp on the dividing wall

explanation_used: One who sides with whoever gives more looks for profit, not justice.
proverb: If you give six, he's on the mother-in-law's side; if you give three, on the daughter-in-law's side

explanation_used: Once one loses honor over a small matter, it cannot be regained however high a price is paid.
proverb: Honor lost over a betel nut won't return even if an elephant is given

explanation_used: Each person has different worries according to their age and situation.
proverb: The grandmother worries about cloth, the daughter worries about marriage

explanation_used: It may mean that the real desire of those who claim love for relatives is for the food and benefit they get there.
proverb: Desire for the rice, love for the relatives

explanation_used: A mocking saying about those who indulge in show and luxury beyond their means even in poverty.
proverb: One to trim the moustache of the man who drinks gruel

explanation_used: It may mean that after so much effort, they didn't get the expected gain in the end.
proverb: One way or another, the sons of Kunti don't have eight kingdoms

explanation_used: Everyone has their own time of authority; it is not permanent, and as time changes, authority changes hands.
proverb: A time for the mother-in-law, a time for the daughter-in-law

explanation_used: The more desires grow, the more sorrow grows; desire is the cause of sorrow.
proverb: Desire is the root of sorrow

explanation_used: It may mean that since many people rushed and fell over one another, nothing was left in the end.
proverb: People fell upon people and the neck became empty

explanation_used: If one admits and repents of a mistake done unknowingly once one knows of it, there is a remedy for it.
proverb: Sin done unknowingly has a remedy once known

explanation_used: The more one loves someone, the more worry and pain there is about them.
proverb: Where there is affection, there is sorrow

explanation_used: One who looks to professional profit won't leave without taking his cut even from his own relatives' work.
proverb: Even if it is his sister's gold, the goldsmith won't leave without stealing

explanation_used: The meaning is not clear; it may be a saying about the irony of someone lacking a necessity getting an unnecessary extra.
proverb: Six bundles of sacred ash for one who doesn't have five bundles

explanation_used: What one desired so much turns out in the end to be a trouble.
proverb: If you marry the one you wanted and wanted, you got a husband who beats

explanation_used: The one who should protect betrays the trust and causes harm.
proverb: Like the fence rising up and grazing the field

explanation_used: Master and servant are both of the same kind of bad quality and are well matched.
proverb: A hemp god, a toddy-drinking priest

explanation_used: In the matter of desires nobody is poor; even the rich have desires.
proverb: There are no poor in desire

explanation_used: Giving authority or responsibility to someone of a harmful nature is dangerous.
proverb: Like giving charge to a scorpion

explanation_used: One who has no worry at all sleeps peacefully even in the noisiest place.
proverb: One without worries sleeps even in the marketplace

explanation_used: It may mean that patience and calmness are a greater virtue than giving charity.
proverb: Patience is greater than charity

explanation_used: Wherever one goes, one cannot escape hardships and sorrows; they must be faced.
proverb: Wherever you go, in whichever direction, sorrow doesn't go away

explanation_used: In the world money carries the most value and respect; everyone honors one who has money.
proverb: Money is the big uncle (money is supreme)

explanation_used: Even if the higher-ups sanction it, the officer or middleman in between creates obstacles and prevents the work from being done.
proverb: Even if the god gives a boon, the priest won't

explanation_used: A distant object or place looks good; its hardships are known only when one goes near.
proverb: The distant hill looks smooth to the eye

explanation_used: It may refer to people who ungratefully measure and find fault even with what was given for free.
proverb: When given as charity for dharma, they went to the backyard and measured it by the cubit

explanation_used: Everyone works for food and clothing, that is, for a livelihood.
proverb: Everyone does it for the belly, for a span of cloth

explanation_used: Glitter and show don't point the true path; truthful speech is the real light.
proverb: Not all light is light; the word of truth is the light

explanation_used: The meaning is unclear; it may be that an action or word directed at one person touches another and affects them.
proverb: If it hits the left crown of the head, it touched the right crown

explanation_used: One who has once met with an accident or trouble is more likely to meet the same trouble again and again.
proverb: A foot that has stumbled stumbles more

explanation_used: It seems to be a parent's lament that at a young age the son has become good for nothing and doesn't listen to what he's told.
proverb: At eight years, my son turned into a stalk

explanation_used: When even great gods are in difficulty, would a lame god get Kailasa? That is, when even the mighty face hardship, it is hard for the weak to get happiness.
proverb: When even such gods are in distress, will a leg-broken god get Kailasa?

explanation_used: Just as one black smudge covers all colors, one big mistake or bad thing hides all the rest of the good.
proverb: All the colors were swallowed by the soot

explanation_used: If everyone sits in the palanquin, who carries it? That is, if everyone wants to be the boss, who will do the work?
proverb: If everyone sits in the palanquin, who will carry it?

explanation_used: Clapping needs two hands; likewise a quarrel or problem involves both persons; one alone is not the cause.
proverb: When two hands clap, there's a sound

explanation_used: 'The blind Dasa who trusted two Dasas was ruined' means that if you rely on two people, each neglects the task thinking the other will see to it, and the one who trusted suffers the loss.
proverb: Trusting two Dasas, the blind Dasa was ruined

explanation_used: One who has risen high must come down one day; that is, power or wealth is not permanent.
proverb: One who has climbed will come down

explanation_used: A husband-and-wife quarrel ends by the time they have eaten and gone to bed; it doesn't last long.
proverb: A husband-and-wife quarrel lasts only until they've eaten and gone to sleep

explanation_used: Like holding on to the tail of the winning ox, an opportunistic nature of joining those who have succeeded and profiting oneself.
proverb: Like holding the tail of the winning ox

explanation_used: Using the Brahmastra to kill a sparrow is excessive; that is, it is not right to take a very big step for a small matter.
proverb: A Brahmastra on a sparrow?

explanation_used: One must winnow grain only while the wind blows and sell when the price is good; that is, use an opportunity at once when it comes.
proverb: Winnow when the wind comes, sell when the price comes

explanation_used: This saying describes an event that happens unexpectedly, without any fuss or confusion and without any warning.
proverb: No fuss or noise at all, Govinda Bhatta fell into the well

explanation_used: It seems to be a saying about empty show of name only: a relationship or position exists only in name, with nothing in reality.
proverb: In name the wife is missing, the son's name is Nanjunda

explanation_used: Like saying 'I came through the window' when told 'Have you gone, ghost?'; even if you drive off nuisances, they come back by another route.
proverb: When told 'Gone, ghost?', it said 'I came back through the window'

explanation_used: When a village is ruined and no one is left, whoever remains becomes the Gowda (headman); when no worthy people are left, even an ordinary person gets a main position.
proverb: In a ruined village, whoever remains is the headman (Gowda)

explanation_used: Drops join into a stream, ears of grain join into a heap of paddy; small efforts or savings add up into something big.
proverb: Drop by drop becomes a stream, ear by ear becomes paddy

explanation_used: Like a grinning Dasa singing the song he already sang again and again; a boring habit of repeating or doing the same thing over and over.
proverb: The wide-mouthed Dasa who sings the same song again and again

explanation_used: The first half means parents find their children dear however they are; the second half is unclear.
proverb: To the parents the bandicoot is a darling, to the companions the monkey is a darling

explanation_used: Everyone else in the house imitates the habit of the eldest brother; elders' conduct affects the younger ones.
proverb: The eldest brother's habit goes to everyone in the house

explanation_used: No one considers the plant in one's own backyard to be medicine; the value of nearby acquaintances or things isn't recognized.
proverb: A backyard plant is not medicine

explanation_used: To use river water that belongs to everyone, the headman's permission isn't needed; for what is open to all, no one's permission is necessary.
proverb: Why the club-wielding chief's permission for river water?

explanation_used: As the washerman at first lifted and beat the sack again and again, one shows excessive enthusiasm at the start of a new task, which doesn't last long.
proverb: In the beginning the washerman lifted the sack again and again and beat it on the stone

explanation_used: An experienced old patient knows more about the disease than a newly arrived doctor; that is, experience is better than fresh book knowledge.
proverb: An old patient is better than a new doctor

explanation_used: Like wearing jasmine flowers on the head though there is no flour to eat; spending on show though there is no money even for basic needs.
proverb: No flour for the belly, jasmine flowers for the hair knot

explanation_used: The god who created us will not let us live by grazing grass; that is, the one who gave life also shows the way to live, so there is no need to worry too much.
proverb: The god who gave birth will make you graze grass

explanation_used: At a chaotic, crazy wedding, the one who ate and left is clever; that is, one who took the benefit he wanted in a disorderly situation is smart.
proverb: At a mad widow's wedding, the one who ate is the clever one

explanation_used: The fiber (thread) joined with the flower also reached the god's feet; through the company of good people, even ordinary ones get good results.
proverb: Along with the flower, the fiber reached heaven

explanation_used: A wish that the festival go well without any trouble, that the house suffer no damage, and that the visiting relatives eat and leave happy.
proverb: Let the festival go well, let the wall be safe, let the visiting in-laws eat and go

explanation_used: If you worry at night, sleep is ruined; if you worry in the day, work is ruined.
proverb: Worry at night ruins sleep, worry in the day ruins work

explanation_used: Telling things as they are angers some people; the plain truth isn't liked by everyone.
proverb: Say it as it is and thunder strikes Siddappa

explanation_used: Like falling by day into a well one saw at night; the folly of getting caught in a danger or mistake despite knowing of it.
proverb: Like falling in the daytime into a well you saw at night

explanation_used: Like holding the nose up even when the whole body sinks in water; not giving up one's arrogance and pride even when completely ruined.
proverb: Even if the whole body sinks, the nose stays up

explanation_used: It may mean that those kept temporarily are not permanent and those wedded cannot easily be abandoned; but the gender and form of the text are unclear.
proverb: Will the one who was merely kept stay? Will the one who was wedded be cut off?

explanation_used: It seems to be a saying that news of the town where one lives shouldn't be spread there, and news of another town shouldn't be told where one has gone; the text is incomplete.
proverb: News of the town you are in shouldn't be raised where you are; news of the town you have left shouldn't be raised where you have gone

explanation_used: When you say things as they are, the listener makes an angry, hawk-like face; telling the truth displeases some people.
proverb: Said it as it was, and the face turned hawk-like

explanation_used: Even the health one had was lost through the effect of the medicine; the remedy tried to fix things and ruined even the good that existed.
proverb: What existed was lost through the medicine's effect

explanation_used: This proverb describes a person who acts big in his own place and stays silent, as if speechless, when he goes elsewhere.
proverb: A headman (Gowda) where he is, deaf where he goes

explanation_used: This saying suggests a state where one's name is spread all over town outside but inside there isn't even basic comfort.
proverb: Kin as far as Ikkeri, but no cloth to cover his shame

explanation_used: This saying says one shouldn't take an extreme step like setting fire to the whole house out of fear of a small trouble.
proverb: Don't set the house on fire because the rats have increased

explanation_used: This proverb says there is no justice when the weak person's enemy is the witness or judge in his dispute.
proverb: A cat as witness in the rat's dispute

explanation_used: Better to live a short time with self-respect than a long time in fear and humiliation.
proverb: Better to live three days as a tiger than a hundred days as a rat

explanation_used: This proverb describes a cheat who, if given a little shelter, grabs the very place the giver has.
proverb: Said 'come here, come here' and he snatched even the house that was there

explanation_used: A saying about a person who doesn't admit defeat even after losing and keeps up his arrogance.
proverb: Though the wrestler fell, his moustache didn't get dirty

explanation_used: This saying suggests people going mindlessly in the frenzy of the crowd.
proverb: Are the people mad or is the fair mad?

explanation_used: This proverb says the importance of money: with money, happiness; without it, hardship.
proverb: If there's money, Kailasa; if not, exile in the forest

explanation_used: This saying says that in life both hardship and happiness naturally come one after the other.
proverb: Hardship and happiness are the two faces of life

explanation_used: This saying criticizes someone who can't handle what is in his hands taking on an even bigger responsibility.
proverb: One who couldn't manage what was in hand took a lease on a kombe tree

explanation_used: This saying points to the senseless justification of claiming to fix the damage from a mistake by profiting from it.
proverb: The sin of killing is remedied by eating

explanation_used: This proverb says a small thing in hand now is better than a big gain that may or may not come.
proverb: A stalk in the hand is better than the bundle inside the mirror

explanation_used: This saying says that a person gains wisdom only after suffering loss or harm.
proverb: Wisdom came after being ruined

explanation_used: A saying meaning that a thing or person small in size is what runs a big system.
proverb: Though the pin is small, it runs the wind

explanation_used: This proverb says the importance of a good reputation: a good name is heaven, a bad name is hell.
proverb: Fame is Kailasa, infamy is hell

explanation_used: This saying warns that the consequences of what is done in anger can't be fixed once one has calmed down.
proverb: Can a nose cut off in anger be restored in peace?

explanation_used: This proverb describes a person who not only ruins himself but ruins those around him as well.
proverb: The monkey not only ruined itself but ruined the forest too

explanation_used: A saying about one who provokes those stronger than himself, gets hurt and suffers.
proverb: A monkey-like fellow provoked, got struck by the pestle, and writhed

explanation_used: This proverb mocks hasty preparation made before the result is known.
proverb: She had the baby's gown stitched before the baby was born

explanation_used: This saying says that however much wealth there is, it gets spent and runs out for those who sit and eat without working.
proverb: A pot of gold is not enough for one who sits and eats

explanation_used: One who patiently bears it even when very angry is truly wise.
proverb: One who holds back when great anger comes is the wise one

explanation_used: It is best to pretend not to see others' faults even when you have seen them; telling what you saw is middling; claiming to have seen what you didn't is bad.
proverb: Not seeing what you saw is best, seeing what you saw is middling, claiming to see what you didn't see is lowest

explanation_used: This proverb criticizes putting others in danger for one's own test or curiosity.
proverb: Like pushing other people's children into a well to see how deep it is

explanation_used: This saying says that however poor or troubled one is, one shouldn't fall into the debt of obligation to others' favors.
proverb: Even if destitute, one should not become beholden

explanation_used: This saying seems to say that a heap of grain can be guarded, but a dead body cannot be kept waiting for long.
proverb: One can guard the threshing floor, but one cannot guard a corpse

explanation_used: This proverb says a daughter leaving her parental home after marriage is as inevitable as a tank overflowing through its spillway.
proverb: A built tank can't avoid its spillway; the house one was born in can't avoid parting

explanation_used: This saying says that to get one's work done, one must bow even before the unworthy.
proverb: To get the work done, hold the donkey's feet

explanation_used: This proverb says that to one who has prejudice or a fault-finding eye, everything looks wrong.
proverb: To the jaundiced eye, everything seen is yellow

explanation_used: Even if sugarcane is crooked, its sweetness is not crooked; that is, though appearance isn't good, quality does not spoil.
proverb: If the sugarcane is crooked, is its sweetness crooked?

explanation_used: Those who make noise do little harm; it is those who stay silent who are truly dangerous.
proverb: A biting dog doesn't bark, a barking dog doesn't bite

explanation_used: This saying expresses the disappointment when what came into one's hand slips away just as it seemed obtained.
proverb: The morsel that came to the hand is not for the mouth

explanation_used: This proverb describes one who shows humility and respect outwardly while holding harmful or deceitful intentions inside.
proverb: A salutation in the hand, a club under the arm

explanation_used: This proverb says that when one thing is needed, the other thing needed with it isn't there; it is rare to get both together.
proverb: When there's a stone there's no dog; when there's a dog there's no stone

explanation_used: Even if camphor is put in a garbage heap, it does not lose its fragrance; a good person does not give up his qualities even in a bad environment.
proverb: If camphor is put in the dungheap, does it lose its own smell?

explanation_used: It may mean that to tell a story you need listeners who say 'hmm', but to live on the right path you need elders who say 'chee' and correct you when you err.
proverb: To tell a story there must be those who say 'hum'; to live upright there must be those who say 'chee'

explanation_used: When the time of ruin comes, the mind doesn't work; at the time of death, no medicine saves.
proverb: No sense at the time of ruin, no medicine at the time of death

explanation_used: Just as one small spark can burn a whole forest, even a small matter can cause great harm or a quarrel.
proverb: A forest can be burned by a spark

explanation_used: Just as the handle of an axe comes from the very tree's clan, if one's own people join in betrayal, the whole kin is destroyed.
proverb: Even the axe's handle is death to its clan

explanation_used: It can be taken to mean that while one person truly suffers, another shows that he suffers just as much.
proverb: The bull buffalo's pain of kosey, the she-buffalo's pain of giving birth

explanation_used: It means the lender becomes meek and laughable, while the borrower takes a fierce form.
proverb: The giver is a clown, the taker is Veerabhadra

explanation_used: One who doesn't know proper conduct and etiquette behaves improperly without regard for place and occasion.
proverb: A dog that had seen no order licked the skull

explanation_used: Making a thing takes much time and effort, but a moment is enough to ruin it.
proverb: A year for the potter; a minute for the club

explanation_used: Having something, even incomplete or of lower quality, is better than having nothing.
proverb: A squint eye is better than a blind eye

explanation_used: This proverb mocks those who build big plans for the future when the basics don't yet exist.
proverb: There's no woman to call 'hey', yet the son's name is Muddu-Ranga

explanation_used: To get ahead in life one must understand the ways of people and the world and learn to account for money.
proverb: Know the world, learn accounts

explanation_used: A sarcastic saying about people who gain comfort or position by bribery and rise through cheating.
proverb: Give a bribe and climb the cot, cheat and climb Kailasa

explanation_used: In a business that brings no profit, however much one works, it is like a donkey scratching its body: only the effort remains, with no fruit.
proverb: Business without profit is like a donkey scratching its body

explanation_used: Even if the meal is a simple greens sambar, one should eat a counted ragi ball without exceeding the measure; keep account and limit even in small matters.
proverb: Even if it's greens sambar, eat a counted ragi ball

explanation_used: Once a bond is severed, the obligation or restriction tied to that bond no longer exists.
proverb: After the lingam is torn, what obligation is there to the Jangama?

explanation_used: One without understanding learns after being beaten; one word is enough for the wise.
proverb: A club blow for the fool, a word blow for the wise

explanation_used: This proverb describes a person who troubles his family but appears good only to outsiders in town.
proverb: A calamity (Mari) at home, a benefactor to the town

explanation_used: It may mean that those who impose themselves uninvited are valued less.
proverb: The one who comes falling on you is last among the three 'kaami'

explanation_used: One who gives up concerns of shame, honor and dishonor gets ahead in the world quickly and influences everyone.
proverb: One who has given up the three is big in the town

explanation_used: This proverb criticizes a hypocrite who keeps bad conduct within but shows himself as pious outside.
proverb: Does wrong, but has a Brindavan in front of the house

explanation_used: One who knows when and how to speak doesn't get into quarrels; one who knows what to eat and how much doesn't get disease.
proverb: One who knows speech has no quarrel; one who knows eating has no disease

explanation_used: Thoughtless speech breaks the family itself; as a stove with a hole is ruined for cooking, even a small defect brings great harm.
proverb: Speech ruined the house, the hole ruined the stove

explanation_used: How hard conducting a wedding and building a house are is known only to those who have done them.
proverb: Perform a wedding and see, build a house and see

explanation_used: It seems this proverb refers to one who gives a funny or irrelevant reply unrelated to what was said.
proverb: When told 'Gunda is getting married', he said 'you yourself are my wife'

explanation_used: One who is charmed by outward beauty and goes near becomes disappointed after learning the inner qualities and drifts away.
proverb: Smitten on seeing the face, moved away on seeing the character

explanation_used: Starting to prepare for a danger after it has come is a late and futile effort.
proverb: They dug a well when the house caught fire

explanation_used: One enemy or trouble should be removed by another enemy or a similar means.
proverb: Remove a thorn with a thorn, remove enmity with enmity

explanation_used: It can be interpreted that if one agrees to everything out of deference, one is finally stuck with no way out.
proverb: Pregnant out of deference, with no place to give birth

explanation_used: A broken pearl cannot be joined again; likewise a word once spoken cannot be taken back.
proverb: A pearl once broken is gone, a word once spoken is gone

explanation_used: A petty person's authority works only within his small sphere, and like the monkey's court at the top of a tree, it has no security.
proverb: The monkey's rule is on the tree branch

explanation_used: A very talkative person, like a pot with holes, cannot hold anything, not even a secret.
proverb: The talkative Brahma is like a pot with holes

explanation_used: It may mean that harm came through our own choice or through our own people.
proverb: Our own eye ruined it for us

explanation_used: Speech sounds like a virtuous person narrating the Puranas, but conduct is rough and bad like a Kirata (hunter-tribesman); saying one thing and doing another.
proverb: Speech ancient, conduct that of a Kirata

explanation_used: To one already immersed in great trouble, the small troubles that come along with it don't matter much.
proverb: What is rain, what is cold, to one who has fallen into the water?

explanation_used: A saying about one who, even after losing or falling by mistake, doesn't admit defeat and shows arrogance and rough stubbornness.
proverb: Even fallen underneath, the nose is up

explanation_used: No matter how much one tries to correct a person of bad nature, his nature does not change.
proverb: A dog's tail is always crooked

explanation_used: No harm comes to the great, or to a good work, just because petty-minded people criticize.
proverb: If a dog barks, is heaven ruined?

explanation_used: Learning good conduct takes as much effort as climbing a hill, but bad conduct comes very easily, like a slide.
proverb: Learning conduct is an uphill rock, losing conduct is a slide

explanation_used: A saying about those who, though they have no real work, run around always acting busy.
proverb: The dog has no work, no time to stand

explanation_used: One who behaves with humility and courtesy achieves victory in life.
proverb: One who becomes courteous will become victorious

explanation_used: It seems to be a proverb meaning that you may invite all the relatives, but shouldn't dip excessively into the money bag in the name of celebration.
proverb: Invite all the relatives, but don't put your hand into the kantale bag

explanation_used: If you state the truth directly, the listener gets angry and the relationship may be spoiled.
proverb: Speaking the truth brings resentment

explanation_used: Those without honesty get no growth or profit.
proverb: No prosperity for those without honesty

explanation_used: Help or a thing not available at the time of need has no value even if it arrives later.
proverb: Pickle that isn't there at mealtime is equal to dirt

explanation_used: This proverb describes partial behavior, treating two people differently: favor for one, harshness for the other.
proverb: Lime for one eye, butter for the other eye

explanation_used: It seems to be a proverb meaning that an act done thoughtlessly in a burst of anger harms oneself.
proverb: If you fall into a well in one fit of anger, you can't get up even in seven fits of anger

explanation_used: Just as fire eats a dry tree, worry melts a living, green person from within.
proverb: Fire eats the dry tree, worry eats the green tree

explanation_used: Whatever comes to one's share, one should accept contentedly, like panchamrita (a sweet sacred offering).
proverb: What comes to one's lot is panchamrita

explanation_used: It seems to be a proverb meaning: whatever happens to something that isn't part of my share, I have no worry about it.
proverb: What does it matter what happens to what isn't in one's share?

explanation_used: It seems to be a proverb meaning that if you step into others' trouble out of pity, their trouble falls on your own shoulders.
proverb: Say 'poor thing' and karma comes

explanation_used: It seems to mean that in trying to avoid sin, one paid a price and brought another trouble upon oneself.
proverb: Bought a curse so that sin wouldn't come

explanation_used: One who ridicules others finally becomes the target of ridicule himself.
proverb: Mocked others and got called a monkey

explanation_used: This proverb says that by the time youth arrives, self-control and discretion are lost.
proverb: When youth came, the measure was lost

explanation_used: Whatever a fortunate person does brings success and profit.
proverb: Everything the virtuous one touches is gold

explanation_used: It seems to be a proverb meaning that even when wealth runs out, desires and demands don't end.
proverb: Though Putya's sorghum is finished, Hotya's song isn't finished

explanation_used: It seems to mean that when an outsider gets a lavish free treat, the member of the house is neglected.
proverb: The free husband ate to his belly's fill, the house husband fell down groaning

explanation_used: This proverb is about those who, not knowing the quality or ability within themselves, wander outside looking for it.
proverb: The civet cat, not knowing its own scent, is said to wander the whole forest and die

explanation_used: No fruit comes from mere talk, preaching or speeches; action is needed.
proverb: If you tell a Purana, will flowers fall?

explanation_used: Knowledge read in a book is not useful in real life without hands-on experience.
proverb: Will the brinjal in the book come to the curry?

explanation_used: It seems to be about one who, though not knowing the right way of conduct, is ahead in giving advice to others.
proverb: Though he doesn't know the manner, he knows the talk

explanation_used: Speech without context or courtesy irritates the listener like a headache.
proverb: Talk without propriety is a headache

explanation_used: There is medicine for illness, but no medicine for a flaw of bad conduct or character.
proverb: There is medicine for disease, there is no medicine for character

explanation_used: Those infatuated by beauty are not afraid of doing wrong.
proverb: Those smitten by beauty have no fear of sin

explanation_used: A saying about one who shows grandeur like a king outside but has beggar-like poverty within.
proverb: Royal pomp is the mark of a pauper

explanation_used: The wife gets comforts and luxuries only as long as the husband lives and earns to support her.
proverb: As long as the king lives, the queen enjoys

explanation_used: Those who have real talent or worth shine wherever they are.
proverb: If the gem is good, it grows in the very place it is

explanation_used: Even those of good qualities, if they fall in bad company, lose their value and respect.
proverb: The bird that eats gems fell in with the crow and became a guest at the leftover leaf

explanation_used: Even the one who wins a quarrel or lawsuit suffers great loss and is as good as defeated; the loser is ruined even more.
proverb: The winner lost, the loser died

explanation_used: This proverb is about an ill-omened person who speaks words of bad portent even when asked to say something good.
proverb: When told 'say something auspicious, Soma', he said 'an owl is visible, uncle'

explanation_used: The ascetic's wife is neither widow nor a woman whose husband lives; it points to a limbo state of being neither.
proverb: The ascetic's wife is neither a widow nor a married woman

explanation_used: Even the ocean of worldly life is only chest-deep water to one who knows swimming; to the skillful, family troubles are easy.
proverb: Worldly life is a river of the ocean; to one who can swim, it's chest-deep

explanation_used: Internal household matters should be kept secret, but illness should not be hidden; it must be disclosed and treated.
proverb: Keep family matters secret, disease matters out

explanation_used: Worldly life is an ocean; one must swim in it, stay there, face the troubles and win.
proverb: Worldly life is an ocean; one must swim, stay, and win

explanation_used: By associating with worldly people, even one who was self-controlled goes astray.
proverb: Associating with a householder spoiled the ascetic

explanation_used: This saying says that however detached one is, everyone has the worry of food.
proverb: Asked what worries an ascetic: the only worry is food

explanation_used: The behavior and attitude of those who have come into wealth change; they are not as before.
proverb: The ways of those touched by wealth are different

explanation_used: Household authority passes to the daughter-in-law and the mother-in-law, once mistress of the house, becomes like a stranger in her own home.
proverb: Home stay for the daughter-in-law, exile for the mother-in-law

explanation_used: This indicates a state of losing freedom and coming under another's control.
proverb: Independence went, dependence came

explanation_used: A saying admiringly claiming that a woman's beauty is the finest beauty and adornment is its essence (rasa).
proverb: A woman's form is the form, adornment is the rasa

explanation_used: In life, sorrow follows joy and joy follows sorrow, again and again.
proverb: Sorrow after joy, joy after sorrow

explanation_used: Even if one must lie, it should be said so firmly, outdoing the truth itself, that everyone believes it.
proverb: Even if you lie, say it as if hitting the crown of the truth

explanation_used: A fraudulent institution fittingly has a fraudster as its head; both are fake.
proverb: A false god, a thieving priest

explanation_used: Using a rare opportunity as an excuse to expect everyone to pamper one and assign no work.
proverb: I've become pregnant, once in a blue moon; don't move, husband

explanation_used: Even if one cannot fully follow one's duty, one should not do a wrong or unethical act.
proverb: Even if you miss your own dharma, don't commit adharma

explanation_used: It describes a state of having lost both options, with no support on either side.
proverb: Both heaven and fort were lost

explanation_used: A state of mere show: everyone has titles and posts, but there's no food actually to eat.
proverb: A title for every head, but ruined with nothing for the belly

explanation_used: It describes the misfortune of another trouble striking one who is already in distress and helpless.
proverb: When the orphan shaved his head, hailstones rained

explanation_used: The sense: one who hasn't succeeded in his own town won't succeed merely by going to another.
proverb: He who cannot live in his own town, will he live in another's town?

explanation_used: One who is a big hero in his own town becomes an unnoticed ordinary person outside.
proverb: A Ranga in his own town, a monkey in another's town

explanation_used: It indicates the situation of getting into trouble oneself while trying to help.
proverb: Went to do a favor, trouble came

explanation_used: One can bear the hardship of hunger, but cannot bear others' harassment and nuisance.
proverb: One can fast, but cannot bear harassment

explanation_used: It indicates an act that gives yet more pain to one who is already hurting.
proverb: Like filling salt into a burning belly

explanation_used: There is no need to wait for an auspicious day to start a business; any day will do.
proverb: What does the day of the week matter for dealing? What does the time matter for trade?

explanation_used: It may indicate a nature that adapts like a doll and, even when falling into trouble, doesn't sink but floats back up.
proverb: Swaying doll, float when you fall into water

explanation_used: A cow that won't give milk and a calf that won't drink it; a state where both sides refuse and the matter doesn't move.
proverb: A cow that won't, a calf that won't eat

explanation_used: It may indicate bringing trouble on oneself by overusing what was found in abundance.
proverb: The forest became fruit, the parrot's mouth got ulcers

explanation_used: A direct piece of advice from an elder: don't be ruined by listening to others; hear my advice and live well.
proverb: Why do you get ruined listening to whose words? Listen to me and live

explanation_used: One cannot know where an unseen danger lies hidden, so one must be careful.
proverb: Who knows which snake is in which anthill

explanation_used: Even if all other seasons fail, the season of death does not fail; death will surely come.
proverb: Whatever season fails, the season of death never fails

explanation_used: Trying to learn when the need arises is too late; one must prepare beforehand.
proverb: Like learning sword-play in the time of war

explanation_used: Wise words should be heard and understood no matter who says them, even children.
proverb: Learn a wise word even from children

explanation_used: One gets to enjoy only as much happiness as is written in one's fortune.
proverb: Enjoyment only as much as destiny allows

explanation_used: Earned wealth gets spent according to the nature of whoever's hands it falls into.
proverb: What the ascetic brought is for the ascetic, what the pleasure-seeker brought is for the pleasure-seeker

explanation_used: A ruler who cannot identify people's abilities fails in his work, like a doctor who cannot identify disease.
proverb: A ruler who doesn't know worth and a doctor who doesn't know disease are the same

explanation_used: It is futile to expect help or hospitality where there is nobody.
proverb: Like going to a town where nobody is and wanting water and buttermilk

explanation_used: Strutting about as a big man where there is no one to question him.
proverb: To a house where no one is, he said 'I am Jogappa'

explanation_used: As the king is, so are the subjects; people follow the leader's conduct.
proverb: As the king, so the subjects

explanation_used: If you tell your sorrow to the wrong person, he gives improper advice suited to his own selfishness.
proverb: When he told his sorrow to his sister's husband, he said 'leave your children and come'

explanation_used: The fruit of what one raised with effort goes to those who don't deserve it.
proverb: Like raising a pumpkin and giving it to the pot-maker

explanation_used: The sense: after everything has gone beyond reach, regret, or going anywhere, is of no use.
proverb: After death, what if he went anywhere?

explanation_used: One who is already powerless or sunk cannot harm anyone.
proverb: Will a dead hen peck at paddy?

explanation_used: Taking on a big undertaking that doesn't suit one's background and qualifications and becoming a laughing stock.
proverb: Like the herdsmen building a monastery

explanation_used: It may mean that one is rock-firm in his stand and the other yields to circumstances.
proverb: The male is a boulder, the female is lame

explanation_used: Men are ruined by laziness, women by excessive frivolity or gossip and laughter.
proverb: The man ruined by sitting, the woman ruined by wandering

explanation_used: When an opportunity or help is there, its value isn't understood; when it is, it has slipped away.
proverb: When the husband was there, no sense; when sense came, no husband

explanation_used: With conversation and company, time and the road pass easily.
proverb: Evening doesn't come without chatter, the road doesn't wear out without company

explanation_used: What is play or fun for one is life-threatening agony for another.
proverb: Play for the cat, mortal agony for the mouse

explanation_used: One who has once tasted profit or pleasure goes back to the same place again and again.
proverb: Like the monkey that tasted sweetness climbing the loft

explanation_used: Not collecting a loan given and not caring for a sown field cause loss; one must keep watch over one's dealings.
proverb: Ruined by not asking for the loan given, ruined by not looking at the field sown

explanation_used: Searching far away without noticing what's close at hand.
proverb: Like keeping the mirror in the hand and looking for the face in the water

explanation_used: A gain or opportunity that had come within reach slips away at the last moment.
proverb: What came to the hand did not reach the mouth

explanation_used: It may mean that everyone makes their own complaint or excuse to suit their own condition.
proverb: A lame cry for one who cries lame, a standing cry for one who cries standing

explanation_used: To one who doesn't understand sense or responsibility, every time and occasion is the same; telling him is useless.
proverb: What is day to a blind man? What is night?

explanation_used: One who, though small in age, is like an elder in understanding and discernment.
proverb: Though small, Shiva's wisdom

explanation_used: It may mean a safe, trusted source is better than an apparently abundant but uncertain one.
proverb: Though there is stream water, well water is better

explanation_used: Water, the basis of life, should be regarded with respect, not neglected or blamed.
proverb: Even if you blame your mother, don't blame water

explanation_used: Even if what one has is ordinary, one should use it well with cleverness and be content.
proverb: Even if it is trash, make it tasty and eat it

explanation_used: A job with respect and security is better even if the salary is low.
proverb: Even if the salary is six kaasu, do palace work

explanation_used: Excessive talk spoils the peace of a house, excessive seed spoils a field; excess in anything is not good.
proverb: Talk increased and the house was ruined, seed increased and the field was ruined

explanation_used: It may mean that those without needed support have neither courage nor the comfort of a home.
proverb: No chest without a bullock, no home without children

explanation_used: One shouldn't do harm to others out of despair, thinking oneself ruined or wronged.
proverb: Don't scatter ruin saying 'I am ruined'

explanation_used: It can be called direct advice: step carefully, humbly, looking at the ground.
proverb: Pat your head and walk looking at the ground

explanation_used: Elders' words may seem bitter (salt) at first but finally bear sweet (jaggery) fruit.
proverb: The head man's word: salt in front, jaggery behind

explanation_used: A father's guidance and support give as much strength as an elephant.
proverb: Father's word, an elephant's strength

explanation_used: Brothers should not be split apart but allowed to stay united.
proverb: Don't separate elder and younger brother

explanation_used: Good health is the greatest wealth a person has.
proverb: Health is wealth

explanation_used: In any task, doing it slowly without haste is what matters and is safe.
proverb: Slowness is the chief thing

explanation_used: There is no age limit for learning; one can learn something new at any age.
proverb: There is no age for learning

explanation_used: When everyone joins together, great strength comes and even a hard task gets done.
proverb: There is strength in unity

explanation_used: Saying a task is easy, but actually doing it is hard.
proverb: Saying is easy, doing is hard

explanation_used: Small drops, when joined together, make a stream flow; small things add up to something big.
proverb: Many drops joined make a stream

explanation_used: Whether a plant will grow well later is seen at the sprout stage itself.
proverb: The prosperity of a growing plant is seen in the sprout

explanation_used: Salt is essential to the taste of cooking; nothing gives as much flavor as salt.
proverb: There is no taste greater than salt

explanation_used: This proverb indicates being moderate and in a middle condition, neither excessive nor very low or poor in any matter.
proverb: The fence is witness for the garden lizard

explanation_used: This proverb says that a plainly visible truth or matter needs no proof or witness.
proverb: Does a sore on the palm need a mirror?

explanation_used: This proverb indicates that a person gains proper understanding or knowledge only after making a mistake or suffering a loss.
proverb: Sense came after being ruined

explanation_used: This proverb indicates that for any big task, quarrel or agreement to succeed or be resolved, mutual cooperation or consensus of two parties is essential.
proverb: Two hands joined make a clap

explanation_used: This proverb indicates a thing or person that exists only nominally or formally and is not counted in real responsibility or calculation.
proverb: Counts for the game, not for the reckoning
